notes.notes: The standard polite greeting all day. Say it when you walk into a shop, a lift or a waiting room.

examples.en: Hello, do you have a free table?

notes.notes: Casual, for friends and people you call 'ty'; also means bye. Hikers often greet each other with it on the trail.

examples.en: Hi, how are you?

notes.notes: Only early in the day, until about nine; after that say 'Dobrý den'.

examples.tl: Dobré ráno, v kolik je snídaně?
examples.en: Good morning, what time is breakfast?

notes.notes: From about six in the evening, for example when you walk into a restaurant.

examples.tl: Dobrý večer, mám rezervaci na sedm hodin.
examples.en: Good evening, I have a reservation for seven o'clock.

notes.notes: Only when someone is going to bed or leaving late at night.

examples.en: Thank you and good night.

notes.notes: Say it when leaving any shop, restaurant or lift. The 'sh' is two sounds: nas-khle-da-nou. Short casual form: Nashle.

examples.en: Thank you, goodbye.

notes.notes: Does four jobs: please, you're welcome, here you are, and 'Prosím?' = pardon? / yes, how can I help?

examples.en: One coffee, please.
– Thank you. – You're welcome.

notes.notes: 'Děkuji' is the more formal spelling; 'díky' is casual thanks.

examples.en: Thank you for your help.

notes.notes: The example is said to a man; to a woman: jste hodná.

examples.en: Thank you very much, you're kind.

notes.notes: Literally 'there is nothing (to thank) for'. A plain 'Prosím' is just as common.

examples.en: – Thank you for your help. – You're welcome.

notes.notes: Polite (vy) form: to get someone's attention or to apologize. To a friend: promiň.

examples.en: Excuse me, where is the metro?

notes.notes: Quick apology when you bump into someone. A woman says 'nechtěla' in the example.

examples.en: Sorry, I didn't mean to.

notes.notes: Literally 'with permission'. What you say to squeeze past people on a tram or in a crowd.

examples.en: Excuse me, I'm getting off.

notes.notes: In casual speech you mostly hear 'jo', and also 'no', which means yes or well, not no!

examples.en: Yes, thank you.

notes.notes: Also 'not' in short answers: Dnes ne = not today.

examples.en: No, thank you.

notes.notes: The adverb of dobrý: 'well', and the everyday way to agree.

examples.en: OK, thank you.
Sorry, I don't understand. Do you speak English?

notes.notes: The question to you is 'Rozumíte?' = do you understand?

examples.en: – Do you understand? – Yes, I understand.

notes.notes: Younger people in cities usually do. Starting with 'Dobrý den' first goes down much better.

examples.en: – Do you speak English? – Only a little.
Sorry, I don't speak Czech.

notes.en: I speak only a little Czech.
accept: I only speak a little Czech.

examples.tl: Mluvím jen trochu česky, mluvte prosím pomalu.
examples.en: I speak only a little Czech, please speak slowly.
Sorry, can you repeat that?
I don't understand. Slower, please.

notes.en: How do you say it in Czech?
accept: How do you say that in Czech?

examples.en: How do you say 'receipt' in Czech?

notes.en: Can you write it down for me?
notes.notes: Useful for addresses, prices and train times.

examples.en: Can you write the address down for me?

notes.notes: Usually dropped, because the verb ending already shows who. Used for emphasis or contrast.

examples.tl: Já jsem z Ameriky. A vy?
examples.en: I'm from America. And you?
Not me, thanks.

notes.notes: Polite 'you' for any adult stranger or staff, and also plural you. 'Ty' is for friends, children and when invited.

examples.en: And you?

notes.notes: The pointing word. 'Tohle, prosím' while pointing gets you almost anything in a bakery.

examples.en: What is that?
This one, please.

notes.notes: 'Zde' is the formal written form you see on signs.

examples.en: Is there wifi here?

notes.notes: On doors TAM means push.

examples.en: The toilets are back there.

notes.notes: Every waiter opens with 'Co si dáte?' = what will you have?

examples.en: What will you have?
A beer and a water, please.
Tea or coffee?
It's nice but expensive.

notes.notes: The next word takes the instrumental: s mlékem, s knedlíkem. Becomes 'se' before s- and z-: se sýrem.

examples.en: Coffee with milk, please.

notes.notes: The next word takes the genitive: bez masa, bez ledu, bez cukru.

examples.en: Tea without sugar, please.

notes.notes: Agrees with the noun: velký stůl (m), velká káva (f), velké pivo (n).

examples.en: One large beer, please.

notes.notes: malý / malá / malé. As the thing you order, the feminine becomes malou.

examples.en: A small coffee, please.

notes.notes: dobrý / dobrá / dobré. For food, 'výborný' = excellent is the stronger compliment.

examples.en: That's a good idea.

notes.notes: Also 'wrong': špatný směr = the wrong direction.

examples.en: That's the wrong train.

notes.notes: Followed by the genitive: hodně lidí, hodně času.

examples.en: There are a lot of people in the center.

notes.notes: Followed by the genitive: trochu vody, trochu mléka.

examples.en: A little more water, please.

notes.notes: With a number or thing it means 'another / more': ještě jedno pivo. Ještě ne = not yet.

examples.en: Once more, please.
Are you still open?
I don't know, I'm not from here.

notes.notes: The easy answer to an apology or to bad news.

examples.tl: – Bohužel nemáme anglické menu. – To nevadí.
examples.en: – Unfortunately we don't have an English menu. – That's all right.

notes.notes: How staff soften a no: Bohužel ne = I'm afraid not.

examples.en: Unfortunately we're full.

notes.notes: Dobrý den works all day and is the usual greeting to staff.

notes.en: I'm fine, thank you. And you?

notes.cue_en: Is this your first time in Czechia?

notes.tl: Ano, moc se mi tu líbí.
notes.en: Yes, I like it very much.

notes.cue_en: What will you have to drink?

notes.en: Yes. I'd like to pay, please.
notes.notes: Zaplatím, prosím is the normal way to ask for the bill.

notes.cue_en: Good evening. Are you checking in?
Could you take a photo of us?

notes.notes: Polite form; to a friend: Jak se máš? Czechs answer it honestly, not just with 'fine'.

examples.tl: – Jak se máte? – Dobře, děkuju. A vy?
examples.en: – How are you? – Fine, thank you. And you?

notes.notes: Literally 'I have myself well'. Short answers: Dobře = fine, Jde to = not bad.

examples.tl: Děkuju, mám se dobře. A vy?
examples.en: Thank you, I'm fine. And you?

notes.notes: Polite form; to a friend: Jak se jmenuješ?

examples.tl: – Jak se jmenujete? – Jana. A vy?
examples.en: – What is your name? – Jana. And you?

notes.notes: Jmenuju se + your own name. Simpler: Já jsem Tom. Formal spelling: jmenuji se.

examples.tl: Dobrý den, jmenuju se Tom a jsem z Ameriky.
examples.en: Hello, my name is Tom and I'm from America.

notes.notes: Said with a handshake and eye contact when you are introduced.

examples.tl: – Já jsem Petr. – Těší mě, já jsem Tom.
examples.en: – I'm Petr. – Nice to meet you, I'm Tom.

notes.notes: Polite form; to a friend: Odkud jsi?

examples.tl: – Odkud jste? – Z Ameriky, ale bydlím v Manile.
examples.en: – Where are you from? – From America, but I live in Manila.

notes.notes: z + genitive: Amerika → z Ameriky. 'Z USA' is said 'z ú-es-á'.

examples.en: I'm from America, from California.

notes.notes: Island groups take 'na', not 'v': na Filipínách, na Havaji. In Manila = v Manile.

examples.tl: Jsem Američan, ale bydlím na Filipínách.
examples.en: I'm American, but I live in the Philippines.

accept: I'm here for the first time.
This is my first time here.
notes.notes: poprvé = for the first time; podruhé = for the second time.

examples.tl: V Česku jsem poprvé a moc se mi tu líbí.
examples.en: I'm in Czechia for the first time and I really like it here.

notes.notes: Here for work = Jsem tady pracovně.

examples.tl: Jsem tady na dovolené, na deset dní.
examples.en: I'm here on vacation, for ten days.

notes.notes: Líbí se mi + thing = I like how it looks or feels: Líbí se mi Praha. For food say: Chutná mi to.

examples.tl: Moc se mi tady líbí, Krumlov je nádherný.
examples.en: I really like it here, Krumlov is gorgeous.

notes.notes: The all-purpose reaction to a view, a square or a church.

examples.en: That view! It's beautiful!

notes.notes: Look each person in the eye as you clink glasses, and don't cross arms. Also said when someone sneezes.

examples.en: Well then, cheers!

notes.notes: Mám rád + thing = I like it in general. A woman says: Mám ráda.

examples.tl: Mám rád české pivo a českou kuchyni.
examples.en: I like Czech beer and Czech food.

notes.notes: Rád + verb = like doing something: rád cestuju (I like travelling). A woman says ráda.

examples.tl: Rád běhám a chodím po horách.
examples.en: I like running and hiking in the mountains.

notes.notes: Liking food and drink only. The waiter or your host asks: Chutná vám?

examples.tl: – Chutná vám? – Ano, moc mi to chutná.
examples.en: – Do you like it? – Yes, I like it a lot.

notes.notes: Even a few words win real goodwill: few visitors try.

examples.tl: Učím se česky, ale je to těžké.
examples.en: I'm learning Czech, but it's hard.

accept: What do you do for work?
notes.notes: Can also mean 'what are you doing?'. Answer: Pracuju jako… (I work as…) or Pracuju v… (I work in…).

examples.en: – What do you do? – I work in IT.

notes.notes: Literally 'how many years are to you?'. To a friend: Kolik ti je?

examples.tl: – Kolik vám je let? – Dvacet pět.
examples.en: – How old are you? – Twenty-five.

notes.notes: Je mi + number (+ let). Swap in your own age: třicet = 30, dvacet osm = 28.

examples.tl: Je mi dvacet pět a bratrovi třicet.
examples.en: I'm twenty-five and my brother is thirty.

notes.notes: Casual versions: Fakt? Vážně? (seriously?)

examples.tl: – Bydlím v Manile. – Opravdu? To je daleko!
examples.en: – I live in Manila. – Really? That's far!

notes.en: Can we say 'ty' to each other?
notes.notes: tykat = use familiar ty, vykat = use polite vy. The older person or the woman offers; don't switch on your own.

examples.tl: – Můžeme si tykat? Já jsem Petr. – Rád, já jsem Tom.
examples.en: – Can we say 'ty' to each other? I'm Petr. – Gladly, I'm Tom.

notes.notes: Friendly goodbye in the polite form. To a friend: Měj se.

examples.tl: Děkuju za všechno, mějte se hezky.
examples.en: Thank you for everything, take care.

notes.notes: Shop staff say it as you leave. Reply: Vám taky = you too. Hezký večer / víkend work the same way.

examples.en: – Have a nice day! – Thank you, you too.

notes.notes: Literally 'happy journey'. You will hear it when you check out.

examples.tl: – Zítra letím domů. – Tak šťastnou cestu!
examples.en: – I fly home tomorrow. – Well, have a good trip!

notes.notes: Casual hi and bye among friends, from Italian ciao. Not for staff or older strangers.

examples.en: Bye then, see you tomorrow.

notes.notes: A woman is an Američanka. The noun is capitalized; the adjective americký is not.

examples.tl: Jsem Američan, ale žiju v Asii.
examples.en: I'm American, but I live in Asia.

notes.notes: A woman friend is a kamarádka. 'Přítel' and 'přítelkyně' usually mean boyfriend and girlfriend.

examples.en: I'm here with a friend.

notes.notes: Declines like an adjective: na dovolenou = (going) on vacation, na dovolené = (being) on vacation.

examples.en: Where are you going on vacation?

notes.notes: ve městě = in town. Staré Město = the Old Town of Prague.

examples.tl: Brno je druhé největší město v Česku.
examples.en: Brno is the second largest city in Czechia.

notes.notes: The short everyday name. v Česku = in Czechia. Čechy = Bohemia (the west), Morava = Moravia (the east).

examples.tl: Jak se vám líbí v Česku?
examples.en: How do you like it in Czechia?

notes.notes: The language as a noun. 'In Czech' is the adverb česky: mluvím česky. Angličtina / anglicky work the same way.

examples.en: Czech is a difficult language.

notes.notes: krásný / krásná / krásné. Even stronger: nádherný.

examples.en: Prague is a beautiful city.

notes.notes: Mild all-purpose praise for things, weather and people. Adverb: hezky.

examples.en: You have a nice view here.

notes.notes: Masculine although it ends in -a. Also means a hiker. A woman is a turistka.

examples.tl: V létě je v centru hodně turistů.
examples.en: In summer there are a lot of tourists in the center.

notes.notes: Changes with gender: jeden lístek (m), jedna káva (f), jedno pivo (n). Counting aloud: jedna.

examples.tl: Jedno pivo a jednu kávu, prosím.
examples.en: One beer and one coffee, please.

notes.notes: dva with masculine nouns (dva lístky), dvě with feminine and neuter nouns (dvě kávy, dvě piva).

examples.en: Two tickets, please.

notes.notes: The ř is a rolled r and 'zh' said together; 'trzhi' is close enough to be understood.

examples.en: I'm staying three nights.

notes.notes: After 2, 3 and 4 the noun is in the ordinary plural: čtyři piva, čtyři lístky.

examples.en: A table for four, please.

notes.notes: From 5 up the counted noun goes into the genitive plural: pět piv, pět minut, pět korun.

examples.en: Five beers, please.
The train leaves at six o'clock.

notes.notes: Usually pronounced 'sedum'.

examples.en: Platform seven.

notes.notes: Usually pronounced 'osum'.

examples.en: Let's meet at eight.
It's nine o'clock.

notes.notes: 11–19 end in -náct: jedenáct, dvanáct, třináct, čtrnáct, patnáct, šestnáct…

examples.en: The train is ten minutes late.

notes.notes: Tens: třicet 30, čtyřicet 40, padesát 50, šedesát 60, sedmdesát 70, osmdesát 80, devadesát 90. 25 = dvacet pět.

examples.en: The toilets cost twenty crowns.

notes.notes: A 50 Kč coin exists; the smallest banknote is 100 Kč.

examples.en: A beer costs fifty crowns.

notes.notes: 200 dvě stě, 300 tři sta, 400 čtyři sta, 500 pět set. Prices reach the hundreds fast: learn these.

examples.en: A hundred and fifty crowns, please.

notes.notes: 2 000 dva tisíce, 5 000 pět tisíc. A 1 000 Kč note is roughly 40 euros.

examples.en: I withdrew two thousand crowns.

notes.notes: Followed by the genitive: půl hodiny = half an hour, půl litru = half a litre.

examples.en: We'll wait half an hour.

notes.notes: druhý = second, třetí = third. Dates use these: prvního května = the first of May.

examples.en: The first street on the right.

notes.notes: Followed by the genitive: kolik lidí, kolik minut. A waiter at the door asks 'Kolik vás je?'

examples.en: – How many of you are there? – Four.

notes.notes: Literally 'how many hours is it?'

examples.tl: – Kolik je hodin? – Je pět hodin.
examples.en: – What time is it? – It's five o'clock.

notes.notes: Answer with v + time: v osm = at eight, ve dvě = at two, v půl osmé = at 7:30.

examples.en: What time do you open?

notes.notes: 1 hodina, 2–4 hodiny, 5+ hodin. Clock: v jednu hodinu, ve dvě hodiny, v pět hodin.

examples.en: The trip takes two hours.

notes.notes: 1 minuta, 2–4 minuty, 5+ minut.

examples.en: The metro runs every three minutes.

notes.notes: Trap: Czech counts toward the NEXT hour, so 'půl osmé' is 7:30, not 8:30. Timetables just print 7:30.

examples.en: Let's meet at half past seven.

notes.notes: On Monday = v pondělí. Many castles and museums are closed on Mondays. Days are not capitalized.

examples.en: The museum is closed on Monday.

notes.notes: On Tuesday = v úterý.

examples.en: On Tuesday I'm going to Brno.

notes.notes: On Wednesday = ve středu: -a becomes -u, and v becomes ve before the consonant cluster.

examples.en: I fly home on Wednesday.

notes.notes: On Thursday = ve čtvrtek.

examples.en: On Thursday we're going to a concert.

notes.notes: On Friday = v pátek.

examples.tl: V pátek večer je v hospodě plno.
examples.en: On Friday evening the pub is full.

notes.notes: On Saturday = v sobotu.

examples.en: The race is on Saturday morning.

notes.notes: On Sunday = v neděli. Small shops may be closed on Sundays.

examples.en: We leave on Sunday.

notes.notes: Spoken form: dneska. Dnes večer = tonight.

examples.en: Are you open today?

notes.notes: Pozítří = the day after tomorrow.

examples.en: Tomorrow we're going to Český Krumlov.

notes.notes: A woman says 'byla jsem' in the example.

examples.en: Yesterday I was at the Castle.
Can I pay now?

notes.notes: Also means 'in the morning' with no preposition. Dopoledne = late morning, odpoledne = afternoon.

examples.en: In the morning I'm going to the airport.

notes.notes: Also means 'in the evening' with no preposition.

examples.en: In the evening we're going for a beer.

notes.notes: 1 noc, 2–4 noci, 5+ nocí. V noci = at night.

examples.en: How much is one night?

notes.notes: 1 den, 2–4 dny, 5+ dní.

examples.en: I'm in Prague for three days.

notes.notes: 1 týden, 2 týdny. Příští týden = next week; víkend = weekend.

examples.en: I'm staying here for a week.

examples.tl: Jak dlouho trvá cesta do Brna?
examples.en: How long does the trip to Brno take?

notes.notes: za + time = that long from now: za hodinu (in an hour), za týden (in a week).

examples.en: The train leaves in ten minutes.

notes.notes: Opposite: brzy = early, soon. Pub kitchens often close by nine or ten.

examples.tl: Je už pozdě, kuchyně je zavřená.
examples.en: It's late already, the kitchen is closed.

notes.notes: Months are Slavic, not Latin: leden, únor, březen, duben, květen, červen, červenec, srpen, září, říjen, listopad, prosinec.

examples.tl: V srpnu je v Praze hodně turistů.
examples.en: In August there are a lot of tourists in Prague.

notes.notes: do restaurace = to a restaurant, v restauraci = in a restaurant.

examples.en: Do you know a good Czech restaurant here?

notes.notes: The classic beer pub with simple hot food. To the pub = do hospody; going for a beer = jít na pivo.

examples.en: In the evening we're going to the pub.

notes.notes: v kavárně = in the café. Cukrárna = a cake and ice-cream shop.

examples.tl: Z kavárny Slavia je výhled na Hrad.
examples.en: From Café Slavia there's a view of the Castle.

notes.notes: Trap: the Czech word 'menu' usually means the fixed lunch set (denní menu), not the list of dishes.

examples.en: The menu, please.
Do you have a menu in English?

notes.notes: Cheap weekday set lunch (soup + main), served about 11–14. Usually on a separate sheet or a board outside.

examples.en: Do you still have the lunch special?

notes.notes: 1 pivo, 2–4 piva, 5+ piv. The default is a half-litre of pale lager; the waiter marks each one on a paper slip.

examples.en: We'll have two beers.

notes.notes: světlé = pale, tmavé = dark, řezané = half and half, nealkoholické = alcohol-free.

examples.en: What beer do you have on tap?

notes.notes: 0.3 litre. 'Velké pivo' is 0.5 litre and is what you get if you just say 'pivo'.

examples.en: One small beer, please.

notes.notes: Trap: 10° and 12° are brewing gravity, not alcohol. Desítka is about 4 %, dvanáctka about 5 %.

examples.en: I'll have a ten-degree.

notes.notes: Pilsner pubs offer three pours: hladinka (beer under a thick foam cap), šnyt (mostly foam), mlíko (all foam).

examples.en: One hladinka, please.

notes.notes: A glass of sweet wet foam, drunk in one go. The word is also everyday Czech for milk (standard: mléko).

examples.en: We'll have a mlíko to finish.

notes.notes: As an order: vodu. Tap water (kohoutková voda) is not automatically offered and not always free.

examples.en: One still water, please.

notes.notes: With voda: perlivá = sparkling, jemně perlivá = lightly sparkling, neperlivá = still.

examples.en: – Sparkling or still? – Still, please.

notes.notes: bílé = white, červené = red. Sold by the decilitre (dvě deci = a glass). South Moravia is the wine region.

examples.en: A glass (two decilitres) of white wine, please.

notes.notes: As an order: kávu. Casual word: kafe (neuter). Espresso, cappuccino and flat white are all understood.

examples.en: One coffee with milk, please.

notes.notes: černý = black, zelený = green, ovocný = fruit. Comes with lemon and sugar or honey, not milk.

examples.en: One black tea, please.

notes.notes: Herbal cola from the communist era, still loved and often on tap. As an order: Kofolu.

examples.en: One draft Kofola, please.

notes.notes: Everyone says 'chleba'. It is wheat-rye sourdough with caraway. Pečivo = rolls and pastries; rohlík = the plain roll.

examples.en: Can I get some more bread?

notes.notes: Menu section 'Bezmasá jídla' = meatless dishes.

examples.en: I don't eat meat.

notes.notes: On menus mostly as the adjective kuřecí: kuřecí řízek, kuřecí polévka.

examples.en: Roast chicken with rice, please.

notes.notes: Short for vepřové maso; the default Czech meat. Declines like an adjective.

examples.en: Is it pork or beef?

notes.notes: Short for hovězí maso. Hovězí vývar = beef broth, the classic starter soup.

examples.tl: Hovězí vývar s nudlemi je klasická polévka.
examples.en: Beef broth with noodles is a classic soup.

notes.notes: se sýrem = with cheese. Hermelín is the Czech camembert; pickled (nakládaný hermelín) it is a pub snack.

examples.en: A cheese baguette, please.

notes.notes: As an order: polévku. Classics: česnečka (garlic), kulajda (dill and mushroom), bramboračka (potato).

examples.en: What's the soup today?

notes.notes: Sliced bread dumpling (houskový) or potato dumpling (bramborový) for mopping up sauce. 2 knedlíky, 5 knedlíků.

examples.en: Bread dumplings with that, please.

notes.notes: In full 'svíčková na smetaně': beef, creamy root-vegetable sauce, dumplings, cranberries. Declines like an adjective.

examples.tl: Svíčková se podává s knedlíkem a brusinkami.
examples.en: Svíčková is served with dumplings and cranberries.

notes.notes: Czech guláš is a thick beef stew with onion, eaten with dumplings or bread: not a soup.

examples.tl: Guláš s knedlíkem a jedno pivo, prosím.
examples.en: Goulash with dumplings and one beer, please.

notes.notes: Breaded fried cheese with fries and tartar sauce: the standard meat-free pub dish. Slang: smažák.

examples.tl: Smažený sýr s hranolky a tatarkou, prosím.
examples.en: Fried cheese with fries and tartar sauce, please.

notes.notes: Breaded pork (vepřový) or chicken (kuřecí) cutlet, usually with potato salad or mashed potato.

examples.en: Pork schnitzel with potato salad.

notes.notes: Sugared dough spiral grilled on a spit, sold all over tourist Prague. Marketed as 'old Czech' but a recent tourist import.

examples.tl: Trdelník se zmrzlinou stojí skoro dvě stě korun.
examples.en: A trdelník with ice cream costs almost two hundred crowns.

notes.notes: Plural word (one fry = hranolek). One portion = jedny hranolky.

examples.en: One portion of fries, please.

notes.notes: Mains often come without one. Pick from 'Přílohy': knedlíky, brambory (potatoes), hranolky, rýže (rice). Charged extra.

examples.en: Which side dish would you like?

notes.notes: 'Účet, prosím' works, but 'Zaplatím, prosím' is more natural. The waiter adds it up at your table.

examples.en: The bill, please.

notes.notes: Round up by about 10 %: say the total you want to pay as you hand over cash or card (bill 183 → 'Dvě stě').

examples.en: Is the tip included?

notes.notes: Menus list allergens as numbers after each dish (1 = gluten, 7 = milk, 8 = nuts).

examples.en: I have a gluten allergy.

notes.notes: pro + number: pro jednoho (for one), pro dva, pro tři, pro čtyři.

examples.tl: – Stůl pro dva, prosím. – Máte rezervaci?
examples.en: – A table for two, please. – Do you have a reservation?

notes.notes: In pubs you share tables: ask before you sit down at one that is half full.

examples.tl: – Dobrý den, je tady volno? – Ano, prosím.
examples.en: – Hello, is it free here? – Yes, go ahead.

notes.notes: For a group: Můžeme si objednat? = can we order?

examples.en: Excuse me, can we order?

notes.notes: Jedno because pivo is neuter. In a pub the waiter keeps bringing more until you say stop.

examples.tl: Jedno pivo a jednu Kofolu, prosím.
examples.en: One beer and one Kofola, please.

notes.notes: 'Ještě jedno?' is what the waiter asks when your glass is nearly empty.

examples.tl: – Ještě jedno? – Ano, ještě jedno, prosím.
examples.en: – Another one? – Yes, one more, please.

notes.notes: Dám si + object form is how you order. Guláš and řízek don't change; feminine -á becomes -ou and -a becomes -u.

examples.tl: Dám si guláš a kamarád si dá řízek.
examples.en: I'll have the goulash and my friend will have the schnitzel.

examples.tl: – Co doporučujete? – Dnes máme výbornou svíčkovou.
examples.en: – What do you recommend? – Today we have an excellent svíčková.

notes.notes: bez + genitive: maso → masa. Careful: 'meatless' soups and sauces may still use meat stock or bacon.

examples.en: Do you have any dish without meat?

notes.notes: A woman says: Jsem vegetariánka. Vegan = vegan (woman: veganka).

examples.tl: Jsem vegetarián. Máte něco bez masa?
examples.en: I'm a vegetarian. Do you have something without meat?

accept: Does it have meat in it?
notes.notes: Je v tom…? = is there … in it? Swap the end: lepek (gluten), mléko (milk), ořechy (nuts).

examples.tl: – Je v té polévce maso? – Ano, uzené.
examples.en: – Is there meat in the soup? – Yes, smoked meat.

accept: I have an allergy to nuts.
notes.notes: na + the thing: na ořechy (nuts), na lepek (gluten), na mléko (milk), na vejce (eggs).

examples.tl: Mám alergii na ořechy. Jsou v tom ořechy?
examples.en: I'm allergic to nuts. Are there nuts in it?

notes.notes: Said by waiters and by everyone at the table before eating. Reply: Děkuju, nápodobně (same to you).

examples.en: – Enjoy your meal! – Thank you, same to you.

notes.notes: The answer to the waiter's 'Chutnalo vám?' = did you enjoy it?

examples.tl: – Chutnalo vám? – Ano, bylo to výborné.
examples.en: – Did you enjoy it? – Yes, it was delicious.

notes.notes: Literally 'I have hunger'. Mám žízeň = I'm thirsty.

examples.en: I'm hungry, shall we go for lunch?

notes.notes: Asked in cafés and bakeries. s sebou = to take away (literally 'with yourself').

examples.tl: – S sebou, nebo tady? – S sebou, prosím.
examples.en: – To go or for here? – To go, please.

notes.notes: Asked at every counter and by every waiter.

examples.en: – Anything else? – No, thank you.

notes.notes: The answer to 'Ještě něco?'

examples.tl: Dvě kávy a to je všechno, děkuju.
examples.en: Two coffees and that's all, thank you.

notes.notes: For a group: Zaplatíme, prosím (we'll pay). You pay the waiter at your table, not at the bar.

examples.en: Excuse me, I'd like to pay, please.

notes.notes: The waiter's question when a group pays. Answer 'Dohromady' (one bill) or 'Zvlášť' (each pays their own).

examples.en: – Together or separately? – Separately, please.

notes.notes: Literally 'that's good'. Say the rounded-up amount, then this, and the waiter keeps the rest. Casual: To je dobrý.

examples.tl: – Sto osmdesát korun. – Dvě stě, to je dobré.
examples.en: – A hundred and eighty crowns. – Two hundred, keep the change.

notes.notes: Prague's is Letiště Václava Havla. To the airport = na letiště; at the airport = na letišti.

examples.tl: Na letiště jede trolejbus 59 od metra Nádraží Veleslavín.
examples.en: Trolleybus 59 goes to the airport from Nádraží Veleslavín metro station.

notes.notes: Never changes in the singular: na nádraží = to or at the station. Praha hlavní nádraží is written 'hl. n.'

examples.en: The train leaves from the main station.

notes.notes: By train = vlakem. České dráhy (ČD) is the state railway; RegioJet and Leo Express are private rivals.

examples.en: I'm going to Brno by train.

notes.notes: Prague has three lines: A (green), B (yellow), C (red). By metro = metrem.

examples.tl: Na Hrad jeďte metrem A na Malostranskou.
examples.en: For the Castle take metro line A to Malostranská.

notes.notes: Feminine: ta tramvaj. By tram = tramvají. In Brno people call it 'šalina'.

examples.tl: Tramvaj číslo 22 jede na Pražský hrad.
examples.en: Tram number 22 goes to Prague Castle.

notes.notes: By bus = autobusem. Long-distance coaches (RegioJet, FlixBus) mostly leave Prague from ÚAN Florenc.

examples.tl: Do Českého Krumlova jede autobus tři hodiny.
examples.en: The bus to Český Krumlov takes three hours.

notes.notes: Never changes its ending. Order one in an app (Bolt, Uber, Liftago) rather than hailing one in the tourist center.

examples.en: We'll take a taxi to the airport.

notes.notes: For transport only. In Prague buy it in the PID Lítačka app, at a yellow machine, or by card on board a tram.

examples.en: One 30-minute ticket, please.

notes.notes: Everyday word for any ticket (train, cinema, concert). 1 lístek, 2 lístky, 5 lístků.

examples.en: Two tickets to Karlštejn, please.

notes.notes: Prague tickets go by time: 30 minutes, 90 minutes, 24 hours, 72 hours. One ticket covers metro, trams and buses.

examples.en: A 24-hour ticket, please.

notes.notes: For trams and buses; a metro or train stop is a 'stanice'. At the stop = na zastávce.

examples.en: Get off at the next stop.

notes.notes: Metro and smaller rail stations. Stanice metra = metro station.

examples.en: At which station should I get off?

notes.notes: Stations give both platform and track: 'třetí nástupiště, kolej pátá' = platform 3, track 5. Check the track number.

examples.tl: Vlak do Brna odjíždí z páté koleje.
examples.en: The train to Brno leaves from track five.

notes.notes: Přestupuju = I'm changing. On the metro, signs saying 'Přestup' lead to the other line.

examples.en: You have to change at Můstek.

notes.notes: Opposite: nastoupit = to get on. Vystupuju = I'm getting off.

examples.en: Where should I get off?

notes.notes: Any trip on wheels: jedu = I'm going, jede = it goes, jedeme = we're going. On foot the verb is jít.

examples.en: Does this train go to Brno?

notes.notes: Paper tickets must be stamped in the yellow box on trams and buses or at the metro entrance. Unstamped = a fine.

examples.en: Don't forget to validate your ticket.

notes.notes: Plain clothes; shows a badge and says 'Kontrola jízdenek'. No valid ticket costs about 1 000 Kč on the spot.

examples.en: The inspector wanted to see my ticket.

notes.notes: PID Lítačka is Prague's ticket app and travel card (PID = Prague Integrated Transport). Activate the ticket before boarding.

examples.tl: Jízdenku si koupím v aplikaci Lítačka.
examples.en: I'll buy the ticket in the Lítačka app.

notes.notes: On boards as 'zpoždění 10 min'. Vlak má zpoždění = the train is delayed.

examples.en: How late is that train?

notes.notes: Station boards: Odjezdy = departures, Příjezdy = arrivals. Airports use odlety and přílety.

examples.tl: Odjezd je v 9:42 z prvního nástupiště.
examples.en: Departure is at 9:42 from platform one.

notes.notes: Of trains and buses; a plane's arrival is přílet.

examples.en: Arrival in Brno is at 11:30.

notes.notes: Compulsory on RegioJet and SC Pendolino trains; optional but wise on busy ČD trains on Friday and Sunday.

examples.en: Do I need a seat reservation for this train?

notes.notes: zpáteční jízdenka = return ticket; jednosměrná = one-way.

examples.tl: Zpáteční jízdenku do Kutné Hory, prosím.
examples.en: A return ticket to Kutná Hora, please.

notes.notes: Literally 'only there'. The ticket clerk's question is 'Zpáteční?' (return?).

examples.en: – Return? – No, one way.

notes.notes: A numbered tram or bus route, or a metro line (also called 'trasa').

examples.en: Which line goes to Florenc?

notes.notes: Platform signs name the last stop: 'směr Háje' = toward Háje. Check it before you board.

examples.en: Take metro line C toward Háje.

notes.notes: Announcement: 'Konečná stanice, prosíme, vystupte' = last stop, please get off. Declines like an adjective.

examples.en: Get off at the very last stop.

notes.notes: In full: cestovní pas. Hotels have to see it at check-in.

examples.en: Here is my passport.

notes.notes: Letadlo = plane, letenka = plane ticket.

examples.en: My flight is delayed.

notes.notes: Board codes: Os = slow local train, R = rychlík, Ex / IC / EC = faster expresses, SC = Pendolino, RJ = Railjet.

examples.tl: Rychlík do Olomouce jede každou hodinu.
examples.en: The express to Olomouc runs every hour.

notes.notes: jedna jízdenka becomes jednu jízdenku as the thing you ask for; do + genitive: Brno → do Brna, Praha → do Prahy.

examples.en: One ticket to Prague, please.

notes.tl: V kolik jede vlak do Českého Krumlova?
notes.en: What time is the train to Český Krumlov?
accept: When does the train to Český Krumlov leave?
What time is the train to Cesky Krumlov?
notes.notes: do + genitive: Český Krumlov → do Českého Krumlova. From Prague you usually change in České Budějovice.

examples.tl: – V kolik jede vlak do Českého Krumlova? – V osm, s přestupem v Českých Budějovicích.
examples.en: – What time is the train to Český Krumlov? – At eight, with a change in České Budějovice.

notes.notes: Platforms are posted only 10–20 minutes before departure: watch the board.

examples.tl: Z kterého nástupiště jede vlak do Plzně?
examples.en: Which platform does the train to Plzeň leave from?

notes.en: Does this go to the airport?
notes.notes: Ask the driver or anyone at the stop. Swap the end: na hlavní nádraží, do centra.

examples.tl: Promiňte, jede to na hlavní nádraží?
examples.en: Excuse me, does this go to the main station?

notes.en: Where do I have to change?
accept: Where do I need to change?

examples.en: – Where do I have to change? – At Florenc.

notes.notes: On ČD trains a paper or display above the seat shows whether it is reserved.

examples.tl: – Je tohle místo volné? – Ano, prosím.
examples.en: – Is this seat free? – Yes, go ahead.

notes.notes: Heard in every metro car: 'Příští stanice: Můstek.' Trams and buses say 'Příští zastávka'.

examples.tl: Příští stanice: Muzeum, přestup na linku C.
examples.en: Next station: Muzeum, change for line C.

notes.notes: The end of the famous Prague metro announcement. You only need to recognize it.

examples.tl: Ukončete, prosím, výstup a nástup, dveře se zavírají.
examples.en: Please finish exiting and boarding, the doors are closing.

notes.en: Where can I buy a ticket?

examples.tl: – Kde si můžu koupit jízdenku? – V automatu nebo v aplikaci.
examples.en: – Where can I buy a ticket? – From the machine or in the app.

notes.notes: Destination + prosím is all a taxi driver needs: Na hlavní nádraží, prosím.

examples.tl: Dobrý den, na hlavní nádraží, prosím.
examples.en: Hello, to the main station, please.

notes.notes: Ask before you get into a street taxi; apps show the price up front.

examples.tl: Kolik to bude stát do centra?
examples.en: How much will it cost to the center?
Stop here at the corner, please.

notes.notes: Said to whoever is blocking the door on a full tram or metro. If you aren't, step aside.

examples.en: – Excuse me, are you getting off? – Yes, me too.

notes.notes: Jedu = I'm going by vehicle. do + genitive for towns: do Prahy, do Brna, do Plzně, do Olomouce.

examples.en: Tomorrow I'm going to Prague.

notes.tl: Platí tahle jízdenka i na tramvaj?
notes.en: Is this ticket valid on the tram too?
accept: Is this ticket also valid for the tram?
notes.notes: Platí = is valid (also 'he pays'). In Prague one ticket covers every mode within its time limit.

examples.tl: – Platí tahle jízdenka i na tramvaj? – Ano, na všechno.
examples.en: – Is this ticket valid on the tram too? – Yes, on everything.

notes.notes: Kde = where (a place). Kam = where to: Kam jedete? = where are you going?

examples.en: Where are we?

notes.notes: doleva = to the left (movement); vlevo or nalevo = on the left (position).

examples.en: Go left at the intersection.

notes.notes: doprava = to the right; vpravo = on the right. Trap: 'doprava' is also the noun for transport or traffic.

examples.en: Turn right and you're there.
Go straight as far as the bridge.

notes.notes: Followed by the genitive: blízko hotelu, blízko centra.

examples.en: The hotel is near the station.

notes.notes: daleko od + genitive = far from.

examples.en: The airport is far from the center.

notes.notes: Mapy.cz is the Czech map app: better than Google for trails and for offline use.

examples.en: Do you have a map of the city?

notes.notes: Left out of most addresses: 'Národní 20'. Street names are adjectives or genitives, so they change: v Nerudově ulici.

examples.en: The hotel is on Nerudova Street.

notes.notes: Written 'nám.' on maps. To the square and on the square are both 'na náměstí'.

examples.en: Let's meet on Old Town Square.

notes.notes: On the bridge = na mostě; across the bridge = přes most.

examples.en: Charles Bridge is full of tourists.

notes.notes: At the corner = na rohu; around the corner = za rohem.

examples.en: The pharmacy is on the corner.

notes.notes: At the intersection = na křižovatce. Semafor = traffic light.

examples.en: After the intersection you'll see the station.

notes.notes: Neuter in -um, which drops off: do centra = to the center, v centru = in the center.

examples.tl: Jak daleko je to do centra?
examples.en: How far is it to the center?

notes.notes: Followed by the dative: naproti hotelu, naproti kostelu, naproti nádraží.

examples.en: The stop is opposite the hotel.

notes.notes: Followed by the genitive: vedle hotelu, vedle lékárny.

examples.en: The ATM is next to the pharmacy.

notes.notes: On foot only: jdu = I'm going, jdeme = we're going, jděte = go (polite command). By vehicle the verb is jet.

examples.en: I'm going to the hotel.

notes.notes: Czech addresses put the number after the street: Vodičkova 12, Praha 1.

examples.en: What is the hotel's address?

notes.notes: Opposite: dolů = down. For position: nahoře = up there, dole = down there.

examples.tl: Na Hrad se jde pořád nahoru.
examples.en: It's uphill all the way to the Castle.

notes.notes: Public toilets often cost 10–20 Kč: keep coins. 'Záchod' is the plain everyday word.

examples.en: Excuse me, where is the toilet here?

notes.en: How do I get to the station?
accept: How do I get to the train station?
notes.notes: Swap the end: na letiště, do centra, na Karlův most, k hotelu (to the hotel).

examples.en: How do I get to the center?

notes.notes: A woman says: Ztratila jsem se.

examples.tl: Promiňte, ztratil jsem se. Kde je Václavské náměstí?
examples.en: Excuse me, I'm lost. Where is Wenceslas Square?

examples.tl: – Je to daleko? – Ne, asi deset minut.
examples.en: – Is it far? – No, about ten minutes.

notes.tl: Můžete mi to ukázat na mapě?
notes.en: Can you show me on the map?
accept: Can you show it to me on the map?

examples.tl: Můžete mi na mapě ukázat, kde jsme?
examples.en: Can you show me on the map where we are?

notes.notes: Hledám + the thing as an object: hledám hotel, hledám lékárnu, hledám stanici metra.

examples.en: I'm looking for the metro station.

accept: Can you get there on foot?
notes.notes: Dá se…? = is it possible to…? pěšky = on foot.

examples.tl: – Dá se tam dojít pěšky? – Ano, je to kousek.
examples.en: – Can you walk there? – Yes, it's not far.

notes.notes: The standard way to give a distance. odsud = from here.

examples.tl: Hrad je odsud dvacet minut pěšky.
examples.en: The Castle is a twenty-minute walk from here.

notes.notes: Zahněte = turn (polite command). You will hear it more than you say it.

examples.tl: Na rohu zahněte doleva a pak rovně.
examples.en: Turn left at the corner and then straight on.

notes.notes: pořád = all the time, still.

examples.tl: Jděte pořád rovně, až uvidíte řeku.
examples.en: Keep going straight until you see the river.

notes.notes: hned = right away, immediately.

examples.en: The metro is just around the corner.

notes.en: Is this the right way to Charles Bridge?
accept: Am I going the right way to Charles Bridge?
notes.notes: Jdu správně na / do / k…? = am I going the right way to…?

examples.en: Excuse me, is this the right way to the station?

notes.notes: The Czech currency (Kč, CZK). 1 koruna, 2–4 koruny, 5+ korun. There are no smaller coins.

examples.en: It costs two hundred crowns.

notes.notes: Not Czech money. Some tourist shops take euros at a poor rate and give change in crowns: pay in Kč.

examples.tl: Jedno euro je asi dvacet pět korun.
examples.en: One euro is about twenty-five crowns.

notes.notes: Plural-only word. Nemám peníze = I have no money.

examples.en: Where can I change money?

notes.notes: Paying in cash = hotově or v hotovosti. Some pubs, market stalls and mountain huts are cash only.

examples.en: I don't have cash, only a card.

notes.notes: By card = kartou. Contactless cards and phones work almost everywhere, including on Prague trams.

examples.en: Do you take cards?

notes.notes: Use a real bank's machine (ČSOB, KB, Česká spořitelna). Avoid Euronet ATMs: poor rates and high fees.

examples.en: Where is there an ATM here?

notes.notes: Trap: '0 % commission' can hide a terrible rate. Ask what you will get first, and never change money on the street.

examples.tl: Ta směnárna u náměstí má špatný kurz.
examples.en: That exchange office by the square has a bad rate.

notes.notes: Compare with the mid rate on your phone. By law you can cancel an exchange within three hours.

examples.en: What's the dollar rate today?

notes.notes: bez poplatku = no fee. Provize = commission.

examples.en: Is there a fee for the withdrawal?

notes.notes: v ceně = included in the price. Prices are written 250 Kč or 250,-

examples.tl: Cena je za osobu, nebo za pokoj?
examples.en: Is the price per person or per room?

notes.notes: In shop windows: 'Sleva 30 %' or 'Slevy'. Studentská sleva = student discount.

examples.en: Is there any discount on it?

notes.notes: As an object: účtenku. Keep the one from an exchange office: you need it to cancel the deal.

examples.en: Can I get a receipt?

notes.notes: v obchodě = in the shop. Malls (obchodní centrum) are open daily, usually until 21:00.

examples.en: The shop is open until eight.

notes.notes: Mostly plural: trhy. Vánoční trhy = Christmas markets; farmářské trhy = farmers' markets.

examples.tl: Na vánočním trhu se platí většinou hotově.
examples.en: At the Christmas market you mostly pay in cash.

notes.notes: Good local ones: glass, garnets, wooden toys, Becherovka, spa wafers.

examples.en: I'm looking for a small souvenir.

notes.notes: Feminine: ta velikost. Clothes and shoes use European sizes.

examples.en: What size are you?

notes.notes: drahý / drahá / drahé. Also means 'dear'.

examples.en: The restaurants on the square are expensive.

notes.notes: levnější = cheaper.

examples.tl: Pivo je tady levnější než voda.
examples.en: Beer is cheaper than water here.

notes.notes: Plural-only: coins. Handy for public toilets, lockers and market stalls.

examples.en: I have no change, only a thousand-crown note.

notes.notes: Free = costs nothing. A free seat or room is 'volný'.

examples.en: Admission is free.

notes.notes: Takes 'si' when you buy for yourself: Chci si koupit… = I want to buy…

examples.en: I want to buy a SIM card.

notes.notes: Platím = I'm paying. For a single payment about to happen: zaplatím = I'll pay.

examples.en: Are you paying in cash or by card?

notes.notes: Visitors from outside the EU can claim VAT back on purchases over 2 000 Kč in one shop: ask for a Tax Free form.

examples.tl: Můžu dostat formulář na vrácení DPH?
examples.en: Can I get a VAT refund form?

examples.tl: – Kolik to stojí? – Sto dvacet korun.
examples.en: – How much does it cost? – A hundred and twenty crowns.

accept: Can I pay with a card?
notes.notes: karta becomes kartou = 'by card' (instrumental, no preposition).

examples.tl: – Můžu platit kartou? – Bohužel jen hotově.
examples.en: – Can I pay by card? – Unfortunately cash only.

notes.notes: Asked at every till. Answer 'Kartou' (by card) or 'Hotově' (in cash).

examples.en: – Card or cash? – By card, please.

notes.en: I want to pay in crowns.
notes.notes: Card terminals and ATMs offer to charge you in dollars or euros at a bad rate: always choose CZK / without conversion.

examples.tl: Bez konverze, chci platit v korunách.
examples.en: No conversion, I want to pay in crowns.

notes.en: How much do I get for 100 euros?
accept: How much will I get for 100 euros?
How much do I get for a hundred euros?
notes.notes: THE question at an exchange office: get the final amount in crowns before you hand anything over.

examples.tl: Kolik korun dostanu za sto dolarů?
examples.en: How many crowns do I get for a hundred dollars?

notes.notes: Berete…? = do you take…? Also: Berete karty? Berete dolary?

examples.tl: – Berete eura? – Ano, ale vracíme v korunách.
examples.en: – Do you take euros? – Yes, but we give change in crowns.

notes.notes: The answer to 'Můžu vám pomoct?' or 'Přejete si?' (can I help you?).

examples.tl: – Můžu vám pomoct? – Děkuju, jen se dívám.
examples.en: – Can I help you? – Thanks, I'm just looking.
OK, I'll take it.
I'll take these two.

notes.notes: Shop prices are fixed and nobody bargains, except a little at flea markets.

examples.tl: To je na mě moc drahé, děkuju.
examples.en: That's too expensive for me, thank you.

notes.notes: Zkušební kabinka = fitting room.

examples.tl: – Můžu si to vyzkoušet? – Jistě, kabinky jsou vzadu.
examples.en: – Can I try it on? – Certainly, the fitting rooms are at the back.

notes.en: Do you have a bigger size?
accept: Do you have a larger size?
notes.notes: větší = bigger, menší = smaller.

examples.en: Do you have it in a smaller size?

notes.notes: Asked at the till; bags cost a few crowns. Answer: Ano, prosím / Ne, děkuju.

examples.tl: – Chcete tašku? – Ne, děkuju, mám batoh.
examples.en: – Do you want a bag? – No thanks, I have a backpack.

accept: Hold your card to the reader.
notes.notes: On card terminals and tram ticket machines. Also: Vložte kartu = insert card, Zadejte PIN = enter PIN.

examples.en: Now hold your card to the terminal.

notes.notes: do hotelu = to the hotel, v hotelu = in the hotel. Stress the first syllable: HO-tel.

examples.en: I'm staying at a hotel by the station.

notes.notes: Small family-run place; the usual stay in Český Krumlov and in the mountains.

examples.tl: Náš penzion je hned u zámku.
examples.en: Our guesthouse is right by the chateau.

notes.notes: 1 pokoj, 2 pokoje, 5 pokojů. In the room = v pokoji.

examples.en: The room is on the third floor.

notes.notes: jednolůžkový pokoj = single room. One big bed = s manželskou postelí; twin beds = s oddělenými postelemi.

examples.tl: Dvoulůžkový pokoj stojí dva tisíce za noc.
examples.en: A double room costs two thousand a night.

notes.notes: 1 klíč, 2 klíče. A key card is 'karta'.

examples.tl: Tady je váš klíč, pokoj číslo dvanáct.
examples.en: Here's your key, room number twelve.

notes.notes: Hotel room or restaurant table. As an object: rezervaci.

examples.en: I have a reservation through Booking.

notes.notes: At reception = na recepci. In small guesthouses it may be staffed only a few hours a day.

examples.en: Leave the key at reception.

notes.notes: Oběd = lunch (the main meal, around noon), večeře = dinner.

examples.tl: Snídaně je od sedmi do deseti.
examples.en: Breakfast is from seven to ten.

notes.notes: 'První patro' is the first floor ABOVE the ground floor (US second floor). Ground floor = přízemí.

examples.tl: Váš pokoj je ve druhém patře.
examples.en: Your room is on the second floor.

notes.notes: Old-town buildings often have none: ask before booking a top floor.

examples.en: Is there an elevator here?

notes.notes: Koupelna = bathroom. In hostels and mountain huts the shower may be shared.

examples.en: The shower is in the hallway.

notes.notes: 1 ručník, 2 ručníky.

examples.en: There are no towels in the room.

notes.notes: Feminine: ta postel. Manželská postel = double bed.

examples.tl: Chtěl bych pokoj s manželskou postelí.
examples.en: I'd like a room with a double bed.

notes.notes: Heslo na wifi = wifi password. Wifi is pronounced 'vifi'.

examples.en: You'll find the password at reception.

notes.notes: One piece; the plural 'zavazadla' is what you normally say for your luggage.

examples.en: I have only one piece of luggage.

notes.notes: 1 kufr, 2 kufry. Also the trunk of a car.

examples.en: My suitcase didn't arrive on the flight.

notes.notes: Klimatizace = air conditioning, which is rare in older buildings and guesthouses.

examples.en: How do you turn on the heating?

notes.notes: The place. The washing itself is 'prádlo'; pračka = washing machine.

examples.en: Is there a laundromat somewhere near here?

notes.notes: Add 'na jméno' + your surname = under the name…

examples.tl: Dobrý den, mám rezervaci na jméno Smith.
examples.en: Hello, I have a reservation under the name Smith.

accept: I would like to check in.
notes.notes: A woman says: Chtěla bych se ubytovat.

examples.tl: Dobrý den, chtěl bych se ubytovat. Tady je můj pas.
examples.en: Hello, I'd like to check in. Here's my passport.

notes.notes: na + length of a planned stay: na jednu noc, na dvě noci, na pět nocí, na týden.

examples.tl: Pokoj pro dva na dvě noci, prosím.
examples.en: A room for two for two nights, please.

notes.notes: Do kolika = until what time. Hotels use the English word; fully Czech: Do kdy musím uvolnit pokoj?

examples.tl: – Do kolika hodin je check-out? – Do jedenácti.
examples.en: – What time is check-out? – By eleven.

accept: I would like to check out.
notes.notes: A woman says: Chtěla bych se odhlásit.

examples.tl: Dobré ráno, chtěl bych se odhlásit, pokoj číslo osm.
examples.en: Good morning, I'd like to check out, room number eight.

notes.en: Do you have a room available?
accept: Do you have a free room?
notes.notes: Signs on guesthouses: 'Volné pokoje' = rooms available, 'Obsazeno' = full.

examples.tl: Máte volný pokoj na dnešní noc?
examples.en: Do you have a room available for tonight?

notes.notes: Works in cafés and pubs too.

examples.tl: – Jaké je heslo na wifi? – Je napsané tady na kartičce.
examples.en: – What's the wifi password? – It's written here on the card.

accept: Is breakfast included in the price?
notes.notes: v ceně = included in the price.

examples.tl: – Je snídaně v ceně? – Ano, podává se od sedmi.
examples.en: – Is breakfast included? – Yes, it's served from seven.

notes.en: Can I leave my luggage here?
accept: Can I leave my bags here?
notes.notes: For before check-in or after check-out; most places say yes.

examples.tl: Můžu si tady nechat zavazadla do odpoledne?
examples.en: Can I leave my luggage here until the afternoon?

notes.notes: Nefunguje + thing covers most complaints: nefunguje sprcha, topení, televize, klimatizace.

examples.en: The heating isn't working in my room.

notes.notes: Literally 'warm water isn't flowing'.

examples.tl: Promiňte, v koupelně neteče teplá voda.
examples.en: Excuse me, there's no hot water in the bathroom.

notes.en: Can you call me a taxi?
accept: Could you call me a taxi?
Can you call a taxi for me?
notes.notes: A taxi called by the hotel is safer and cheaper than one hailed on the street.

examples.tl: Můžete mi zavolat taxi na šestou ráno?
examples.en: Can you call me a taxi for six in the morning?

notes.en: Can I get one more towel?
notes.notes: Můžu dostat ještě + thing = can I get another…? Feminine things: ještě jednu deku (blanket).

examples.en: Can I get one more pillow?

notes.notes: On doors, in shops and stations. Also the word for 'east' and for an airport gate.

examples.tl: Sejdeme se u východu z metra.
examples.en: Let's meet at the metro exit.

notes.notes: One syllable away from východ (exit): v- = in, vý- = out. 'Vstup' is also used for entry.

examples.en: The entrance is on the other side.

notes.notes: On doors: TAM = push (literally 'there', away from you). SEM = pull.

examples.en: The door says PUSH.

notes.notes: On doors: SEM = pull (literally 'to here', toward you). Also: Pojďte sem = come here.

examples.en: SEM means pull, TAM means push.

notes.notes: On shop doors, often with hours: Otevřeno 9–18. 'Nonstop' = open 24 hours.

examples.tl: Otevřeno denně od devíti do šesti.
examples.en: Open daily from nine to six.

notes.notes: On doors. 'Z technických důvodů zavřeno' = closed for technical reasons.

examples.en: Closed on Mondays.

notes.notes: Smoking is banned inside pubs and restaurants and at stops. Zákaz = ban: zákaz vstupu, zákaz focení.

examples.en: Smoking is banned in the restaurant.

notes.notes: Plural on signs (one = toaleta); also 'WC', said 'vé-cé'. Often paid: 10–20 Kč at stations and in malls.

examples.en: The toilets are on the ground floor.

notes.notes: On toilet doors (plural of muž = man). Often just M. Careful: Ž is the women's.

examples.en: Toilets: men on the left, women on the right.

notes.notes: On toilet doors (plural of žena = woman). Often just Ž.

examples.tl: Dveře s písmenem Ž jsou pro ženy.
examples.en: The door with the letter Ž is for women.

notes.notes: The other men's toilet sign (plural of pán). Older places use this pair: Páni / Dámy.

examples.en: The door says Gentlemen.

notes.notes: The other women's toilet sign (plural of dáma).

examples.tl: Toalety pro dámy jsou v prvním patře.
examples.en: The ladies' toilets are on the first floor.

notes.notes: On boards as 'Nást.' At the platform = na nástupišti; from platform 3 = z třetího nástupiště. The track is 'kolej'.

examples.tl: Vlak do Brna odjíždí z třetího nástupiště.
examples.en: The train to Brno leaves from platform three.

notes.notes: On warning signs: Pozor, schod (step); Pozor, zlý pes (fierce dog). Shouted: Pozor! = look out!

examples.en: Mind the step!

notes.notes: Wherever you pay: station ticket windows, a castle box office, a supermarket checkout.

examples.tl: Vstupenky koupíte v pokladně u vchodu.
examples.en: You can buy tickets at the ticket office by the entrance.

notes.notes: In the metro 'Výstup' marks the way up to the street, with street names. Also means getting off a vehicle.

examples.tl: Výstup do ulice Na Příkopě je vpravo.
examples.en: The way out to Na Příkopě street is on the right.

notes.notes: Metro signs: 'Přestup na linku C' = change to line C. In timetables: s přestupem = with a change.

examples.tl: Přestup na linku B je na Můstku.
examples.en: The transfer to line B is at Můstek.

notes.notes: Green signs; also 'únikový východ' (escape exit).

examples.tl: Nouzový východ je na konci chodby.
examples.en: The emergency exit is at the end of the hallway.

notes.notes: Also 'Zákaz vstupu' or 'Nepovolaným vstup zakázán' (no unauthorized entry).

examples.tl: Tady je vstup zakázán, musíme jít jinudy.
examples.en: There's no entry here, we have to go another way.

notes.notes: On lifts, escalators, ATMs and ticket machines.

examples.en: The elevator is out of order.

notes.notes: On ticket sites and concert posters, and on RegioJet connections in summer.

examples.en: Today's tour is sold out.

notes.notes: On toilet locks, car-park boards and guesthouse doors. A waiter says it when every table is taken.

examples.en: Unfortunately everything is taken.

notes.notes: Opposite of obsazeno: on toilet locks and car parks. 'Volné pokoje' = rooms available.

examples.en: There's still room by the window.

notes.notes: On pub doors and stalls: 'Platba pouze v hotovosti' or 'Karty nebereme' (we don't take cards).

examples.en: Payment in cash only.

notes.notes: Short for koruna česká, written after the number: 250 Kč or 250,-. The comma is the decimal mark: 49,90 Kč.

examples.en: Admission 250 crowns, children 150 crowns.

notes.notes: Plural-only: the sign over small food shops. A 'večerka' is a corner shop open late.

examples.tl: Potraviny na rohu mají otevřeno do deseti.
examples.en: The grocery store on the corner is open until ten.

notes.notes: On price tags and in windows: Akce! = on offer. Also means an event. Výprodej = clearance sale.

examples.en: Beer is on offer today.

notes.notes: On fountains and taps. 'Voda není pitná' or 'Nepitná voda' = do not drink.

examples.en: Is this drinking water?

notes.notes: At main stations, staffed or as lockers (úložné skříňky). Handy between check-out and a late train.

examples.tl: Úschovna zavazadel je v přízemí nádraží.
examples.en: The left luggage office is on the ground floor of the station.

notes.notes: On tram and bus stop signs and timetables: the vehicle stops only if you press the button or wave.

examples.tl: Tahle zastávka je na znamení, zmáčkněte tlačítko.
examples.en: This is a request stop, press the button.

notes.notes: Opening-hours shorthand: Po, Út, St, Čt, Pá, So, Ne = Monday to Sunday. 'Denně' = daily.

examples.en: Open Mon–Fri 8–18, Sat 9–12.

notes.notes: A fortified medieval castle. Pražský hrad = Prague Castle: na Hrad = to the Castle, na Hradě = at the Castle.

examples.tl: Vstup do areálu Pražského hradu je zdarma.
examples.en: Entry to the grounds of Prague Castle is free.

notes.notes: A residential palace (Český Krumlov, Lednice), not a fortress like a 'hrad'. Also means a lock.

examples.tl: Zámek v Českém Krumlově má krásnou věž.
examples.en: The chateau in Český Krumlov has a beautiful tower.

notes.notes: v kostele = in the church. A grand one is a chrám or katedrála; a chapel is a kaple.

examples.tl: Ten kostel je ze čtrnáctého století.
examples.en: That church is from the fourteenth century.

notes.notes: The big one is Katedrála svatého Víta (St. Vitus) inside Prague Castle.

examples.tl: Katedrála svatého Víta je na Pražském hradě.
examples.en: St. Vitus Cathedral is at Prague Castle.

notes.notes: Neuter in -um, which drops off: do muzea = to the museum, v muzeu = in the museum.

examples.tl: Národní muzeum je na Václavském náměstí.
examples.en: The National Museum is on Wenceslas Square.

notes.notes: Feminine: ta věž. Up the tower = na věž.

examples.tl: Dá se jít nahoru na věž?
examples.en: Can you go up the tower?

notes.notes: Plural: památky = the sights. Památka UNESCO = UNESCO site (Prague, Český Krumlov, Kutná Hora, Telč).

examples.tl: Jaké památky jsou tady v okolí?
examples.en: What sights are there around here?

notes.notes: A ticket for a sight, concert or match. A transport ticket is a jízdenka.

examples.en: Tickets can be bought online.

notes.notes: Declines like an adjective. Snížené vstupné = reduced price (students, seniors).

examples.en: How much is admission?

notes.notes: Most castle interiors can only be seen on a timed guided tour: book the English one or ask for a printed text.

examples.en: What time does the next tour start?

notes.notes: Masculine although it ends in -e; a woman guide is a průvodkyně. Also means a guidebook.

examples.en: The tour is only with a guide.

notes.notes: Posted on doors and websites. Winter hours are shorter, and many castles close from November to March.

examples.en: What are the opening hours?

notes.notes: Most town squares have one with a tower you can climb.

examples.en: The astronomical clock is on the Old Town Hall.

notes.notes: The Prague Orloj on Old Town Square: the apostles parade every hour from 9:00 to 23:00.

examples.tl: V poledne je u orloje plno.
examples.en: At noon it's packed at the astronomical clock.

notes.notes: výhled na + thing: na město, na Hrad, na řeku. Vyhlídka = a viewpoint.

examples.tl: Z věže je krásný výhled na město.
examples.en: From the tower there's a beautiful view of the city.

notes.notes: As an object: fotku. Formal word: fotografie.

examples.en: Can I take a photo?

notes.notes: Tours: Plzeňský Prazdroj in Plzeň, Budvar in České Budějovice, Staropramen in Prague.

examples.en: The brewery tour ends with a tasting.

notes.notes: The adjective follows the thing: Jak je ten kostel starý? Jak je ta věž stará?

examples.tl: – Jak je ten most starý? – Skoro sedm set let.
examples.en: – How old is that bridge? – Almost seven hundred years.

notes.notes: Předpověď počasí = weather forecast.

examples.en: The weather is beautiful today.

notes.notes: The stem changes: v dešti = in the rain. Deštník = umbrella.

examples.en: Rain is supposed to come in the afternoon.

notes.notes: The stem changes: na sněhu = on the snow. Sněží = it's snowing.

examples.en: There's already snow in the mountains.

notes.notes: dvě, not dva, because vstupenka is feminine. For one: Jednu vstupenku, prosím.

examples.en: One adult ticket, please.

notes.notes: V kolik otevíráte? = what time do you open? Last entry is often an hour before closing.

examples.tl: – V kolik zavíráte? – V pět, poslední vstup je ve čtyři.
examples.en: – What time do you close? – At five, last entry is at four.

notes.notes: Worth asking: most castles, chateaux and many museums are closed on Mondays.

examples.tl: – Máte otevřeno v pondělí? – Ne, v pondělí je zavřeno.
examples.en: – Are you open on Monday? – No, we're closed on Mondays.

notes.notes: Photos are often banned on castle interior tours. Sign: Zákaz focení = no photography.

examples.tl: – Může se tady fotit? – Ano, ale bez blesku.
examples.en: – Can you take photos here? – Yes, but without flash.

accept: Can you take a photo of us?
notes.notes: Just you: Můžete mě vyfotit? = can you take my picture?

examples.en: Excuse me, can you take our picture?

notes.notes: If not, ask for the printed text: Máte text v angličtině?

examples.tl: – Je prohlídka v angličtině? – V angličtině je ve dvě hodiny.
examples.en: – Is the tour in English? – The English one is at two o'clock.

notes.en: What will the weather be tomorrow?
accept: What will the weather be like tomorrow?
notes.notes: bude = will be.

examples.tl: – Jaké bude zítra počasí? – Má být hezky.
examples.en: – What will the weather be tomorrow? – It's supposed to be nice.

notes.notes: One word, no 'it'. Sněží = it's snowing, fouká = it's windy, svítí slunce = the sun is shining.

examples.en: It's raining, let's go to a museum.

notes.notes: Zima also means winter. I'm cold = Je mi zima. Je teplo = it's warm, je horko = it's hot.

examples.tl: Na hřebenech je zima i v létě.
examples.en: On the ridges it's cold even in summer.

notes.notes: Shout 'Pomoc!' in an emergency. The EU emergency number is 112; operators speak English.

examples.en: Help! Thief!

notes.notes: Dial 158 or 112. Městská policie = city police, for minor matters. Policejní stanice = police station.

examples.en: I have to report it to the police.

notes.notes: Formal word: lékař. A woman doctor is doktorka / lékařka. Addressing one: pane doktore, paní doktorko.

examples.tl: Je tady někde doktor, který mluví anglicky?
examples.en: Is there a doctor around here who speaks English?

notes.notes: To hospital = do nemocnice; in hospital = v nemocnici. The emergency room is 'pohotovost'.

examples.en: I have to go to the hospital.

notes.notes: Green cross sign. This is where you buy medicine, even basic painkillers; a 'drogerie' mostly sells toiletries.

examples.en: The pharmacy is open until six.

notes.notes: Dial 155 or 112. The service itself is called 'záchranka' (záchranná služba).

examples.en: The ambulance will arrive in five minutes.

notes.notes: 1 lék, 2 léky. Na předpis = prescription only; bez předpisu = over the counter.

examples.en: I need medicine for a fever.

notes.notes: Feminine: ta bolest. Bolest hlavy = headache, bolest zubů = toothache.

examples.en: It's a sharp pain.

notes.notes: A woman says 'uhodila jsem se' in the example.

examples.en: I hit my head.

notes.notes: Bolí mě břicho = I have a stomach ache. Žaludek is the organ itself.

examples.en: My stomach has been hurting since this morning.

notes.notes: Covers both leg and foot. Plural: nohy. Kotník = ankle, koleno = knee.

examples.en: I injured my leg.

notes.notes: Plural-only neuter word: bolí mě záda = my back hurts.

examples.en: My back hurts after the trip.

notes.notes: Mám horečku = I have a fever. Temperatures are in Celsius: 38 °C is about 100 °F.

examples.tl: Mám horečku a bolí mě v krku.
examples.en: I have a fever and a sore throat.

notes.notes: Jsem nachlazený = I have a cold (woman: nachlazená). Rýma = runny nose, chřipka = flu.

examples.en: Do you have something for a cold?

notes.notes: Sirup na kašel = cough syrup.

examples.en: I've had a cough for three days.

notes.notes: Zvracet = to vomit. Tap water is safe to drink everywhere in Czechia.

examples.tl: Mám průjem, potřebuju něco z lékárny.
examples.en: I have diarrhea, I need something from the pharmacy.

notes.notes: Jsem nemocný (woman: nemocná). For feeling sick right now say: Je mi špatně.

examples.tl: Jsem nemocný, zůstanu dnes v hotelu.
examples.en: I'm sick, I'll stay at the hotel today.

notes.notes: Cestovní pojištění = travel insurance. A clinic will ask for it or for payment up front.

examples.en: I have travel insurance.

notes.notes: As an object: peněženku.

examples.en: I can't find my wallet.

notes.notes: Watch your bag on tram 22, on Charles Bridge, at the Orloj and in crowded metro stations. Zloděj = thief.

examples.en: Watch out for pickpockets on the tram.

notes.notes: Official word: velvyslanectví. The US Embassy is in Malá Strana in Prague.

examples.en: Where is the American embassy?

notes.notes: Potřebuju = I need (formal spelling: potřebuji). Softer: Můžete mi pomoct? = can you help me?

examples.en: Excuse me, I need help. Do you speak English?

notes.notes: sanitka becomes sanitku as the object. Or dial 155 / 112 yourself.

examples.en: Quick, call an ambulance!

notes.notes: policie becomes policii as the object.

examples.en: I've been robbed, call the police!

notes.notes: doktor becomes doktora: masculine words for people add -a as the object.

examples.en: My friend needs a doctor.

notes.notes: Bolí mě + body part: bolí mě břicho, zub (tooth), v krku (throat), záda (back).

examples.tl: Bolí mě hlava, máte nějaký prášek?
examples.en: I have a headache, do you have a pill?

notes.notes: Literally 'it is badly to me': nausea or feeling unwell. Je mi líp = I feel better.

examples.tl: Je mi špatně, potřebuju na vzduch.
examples.en: I feel sick, I need some air.

notes.notes: nejbližší = nearest: nejbližší nemocnice, nejbližší bankomat, nejbližší stanice metra.

examples.en: Where is the nearest hospital?

notes.notes: A woman says: Ztratila jsem pas. Report it to the police, then contact your embassy.

examples.en: I lost my passport and my wallet.

notes.notes: Literally 'they stole from me'. Swap the thing: Ukradli mi telefon / batoh / pas.

examples.en: My phone was stolen on the tram.

notes.en: Do you have something for pain?
accept: Do you have anything for pain?
notes.notes: na + the problem: na bolest hlavy, na kašel, na horečku, na průjem, na alergii.

examples.en: Do you have something for a headache?

notes.notes: A woman says: Jsem alergická na penicilin.

examples.tl: Jsem alergický na penicilin a na ořechy.
examples.en: I'm allergic to penicillin and to nuts.

notes.notes: The doctor's question. Answer by pointing and saying 'Tady' = here.

examples.tl: – Kde to bolí? – Tady, v koleni.
examples.en: – Where does it hurt? – Here, in my knee.

notes.notes: Literally 'it's burning'. Fire brigade (hasiči): 150 or 112.

examples.en: Fire! Everybody out!

notes.notes: Firm but in the polite form. With pushy touts a plain 'Ne, děkuju' while walking on usually works.

examples.en: I don't want it, leave me alone!

notes.notes: na túru = (going) on a hike. Výlet = a day trip of any kind.

examples.tl: Zítra jdeme na túru na Sněžku.
examples.en: Tomorrow we're going on a hike up Sněžka.

notes.notes: Mostly plural: hory. To the mountains = na hory; in the mountains = na horách.

examples.en: At the weekend we're going to the mountains.

notes.notes: na vrchol = to the summit, na vrcholu = on the summit. Sněžka (1 603 m) is the highest in Czechia.

examples.en: It's very windy on the summit.

notes.notes: Mountain hut with beds, beer and hot food; in the Krkonoše it is a 'bouda'. Also a weekend cottage.

examples.tl: Na chatě si dáme polévku a pivo.
examples.en: At the hut we'll have soup and a beer.

notes.notes: A coloured stripe between two white ones on trees and rocks. Red = main long routes, then blue, green, yellow.

examples.tl: Jděte pořád po červené turistické značce.
examples.en: Keep following the red trail marker.

notes.notes: Arrow signs at trail junctions listing destinations with distances in km. The junction itself is a 'rozcestí'.

examples.tl: Na rozcestníku je napsáno: Sněžka 3 km.
examples.en: The signpost says: Sněžka 3 km.

notes.notes: Naučná stezka = nature trail with info boards; cyklostezka = bike path. Any route is also a 'cesta'.

examples.en: The trail leads through the forest to the waterfall.

notes.notes: po + colour: po červené (red), po modré (blue), po zelené (green), po žluté (yellow).

examples.tl: Na vrchol jděte po červené, zpátky po modré.
examples.en: Take the red trail to the summit and the blue one back.

notes.notes: Czech hills are dotted with them; a small fee, often cash, to climb. Petřín in Prague is the famous one.

examples.tl: Z rozhledny je vidět až do Polska.
examples.en: From the lookout tower you can see as far as Poland.

notes.notes: Covers cable cars, chairlifts and funiculars. By cable car = lanovkou.

examples.tl: Na Sněžku jede lanovka z Pece pod Sněžkou.
examples.en: A cable car goes up Sněžka from Pec pod Sněžkou.

notes.notes: Start and cíl (finish) are on every race map. Úschovna = bag drop.

examples.tl: – Kde je start? – Na náměstí, v devět hodin.
examples.en: – Where is the start? – On the square, at nine o'clock.

notes.notes: Summer afternoon storms are common in the mountains: start early and get off the ridge in time.

examples.en: There are supposed to be thunderstorms in the afternoon.

notes.tl: Jak dlouho se jde na vrchol?
notes.en: How long is the walk to the top?
accept: How long does it take to the summit?
How long is the hike to the summit?
notes.notes: se jde = one walks. Swap the end: na chatu (to the hut), k lanovce (to the cable car).

examples.tl: – Jak dlouho se jde na vrchol? – Asi dvě hodiny.
examples.en: – How long is the walk to the top? – About two hours.

notes.notes: těžký = difficult or heavy; lehký = easy or light; prudký = steep.

examples.tl: – Je ta cesta těžká? – Ne, jen ke konci je prudká.
examples.en: – Is the trail difficult? – No, it's only steep toward the end.

notes.notes: Check the mountain rescue (Horská služba) forecast before a ridge walk.

examples.tl: Kazí se počasí, radši se vrátíme.
examples.en: The weather is turning, we'd better go back.

notes.notes: Both the sport and a running event. Going for a run = jít si zaběhat.

examples.tl: Ráno si jdu zaběhat podél řeky.
examples.en: In the morning I'm going for a run along the river.

notes.notes: běžím = I'm running (now, or a race); běhat is the habit: běhám třikrát týdně = I run three times a week.

examples.en: Tomorrow I'm running a half marathon.

notes.notes: 1 závod, 2 závody. Big ones in Prague: the půlmaraton in spring and the maraton in May.

examples.tl: V sobotu běžím závod na deset kilometrů.
examples.en: On Saturday I'm running a ten-kilometre race.

notes.notes: The banner over the finish line says CÍL; the start is START. Also 'destination' in navigation apps.

examples.en: Two kilometres to go to the finish.

notes.prompt: Say it politely, as a man: ___ jedno pivo. (I would like one beer.)
notes.explanation: Chtěl bych + thing or verb is the polite 'I would like'. A woman says Chtěla bych. Plain Chci (I want) sounds blunt to staff.

notes.prompt: Ask where it is: ___ nádraží? (Where is the station?)
notes.explanation: Kde je + the place in its dictionary form. For plural things use Kde jsou: Kde jsou toalety?

notes.prompt: Ask permission: ___ platit kartou? (Can I pay by card?)
notes.explanation: Můžu + infinitive = can I / may I. Formal spelling: mohu. Můžeme = can we.

notes.prompt: Ask a stranger for help: ___ mi pomoct? (Can you help me?)
notes.explanation: Můžete + infinitive is the polite request to staff and strangers: Můžete mi to napsat? Even softer: Mohl byste…?

notes.prompt: Ask staff whether they have it: ___ wifi? (Do you have wifi?)
notes.explanation: Máte + thing asks any shop, hotel or restaurant: Máte volný stůl? Máte mapu? The answer is Máme (we have) or Nemáme.

notes.prompt: Order it: Dám si ___. (I'll have the soup; soup = polévka)
notes.explanation: Feminine nouns in -a switch to -u when they are the thing you want, order or look for: káva → kávu, voda → vodu, jízdenka → jízdenku.

notes.prompt: Make it negative: mluvím česky (I speak Czech) → ___ česky
notes.explanation: Stick ne- onto the front of the verb, as one word: nemám, nechci, nevím, nerozumím. 'Is not' is irregular: není.

notes.prompt: Two of a neuter noun: ___ piva, prosím. (Two beers, please.)
notes.explanation: Dva goes with masculine nouns (dva lístky, dva čaje); dvě with feminine and neuter nouns (dvě kávy, dvě piva).

notes.prompt: Count five or more: pět ___ (five beers; beer = pivo)
notes.explanation: 1 pivo, 2–4 piva, but from 5 up the noun goes into the genitive plural: pět piv, deset minut, sto korun, pět lístků.

notes.prompt: To a town or into a place: do ___ (to the center; center = centrum)
notes.explanation: do + genitive = to / into: do centra, do Prahy, do Brna, do hotelu, do muzea, do hospody.

notes.prompt: Some places take a different 'to': Jedu ___ letiště. (I'm going to the airport.)
notes.explanation: Use na, not do, with letiště, nádraží, náměstí, zastávka, Hrad, pošta, koncert, pivo: na nádraží, na Hrad, na pivo.

notes.prompt: Say where you are: Jsem v ___. (I'm in Prague; Prague = Praha)
notes.explanation: Being somewhere takes the locative: Praha → v Praze, Brno → v Brně, Krumlov → v Krumlově, hotel → v hotelu.

notes.prompt: With something: káva s ___ (coffee with milk; milk = mléko)
notes.explanation: s + instrumental: masculine and neuter nouns add -em (s mlékem, s knedlíkem, s ledem); feminine -a becomes -ou (se zmrzlinou).

notes.prompt: Past tense, a man speaking: Včera ___ na Hradě. (Yesterday I was at the Castle.)
notes.explanation: Past = the -l form + jsem, and jsem always sits in second place: Byl jsem tam. / Včera jsem tam byl. A woman says byla.

notes.prompt: Talk about tomorrow: Zítra ___ v Brně. (Tomorrow I will be in Brno.)
notes.explanation: Budu = I will be; budu + infinitive = I will do: budu čekat. Often the present plus zítra is enough: Zítra jedu do Brna.
